thread:
andrew: Hit a nasty one on the edge build — our web app bundles ~1.2MB of extra polyfills after upgrading the JS SDK. bundle analyzer shows node builtin polyfills (crypto, buffer) pulled in. deploy failed on Vercel Edge with "ReferenceError: global is not defined".

andrew: stack (abridged):
```
TypeError: crypto.createHash is not a function
    at newHasher (node_modules/redwood-js-sdk/dist/index.cjs.js:234:12)
    at init (app/edge-entry.js:12:7)
```

samira: ugh. likely CJS entry is dragging a commonjs-only helper or a polyfill path that bundlers can't tree-shake. did you check package.json exports/sideEffects?

andrew: package.json has both `main` (cjs) and `module` (esm) but we ship a single dist/index.js that re-exports everything. sideEffects is absent.

leo: try marking "sideEffects": false and ensure files with runtime polyfills are listed in exports only when needed. bundlers like webpack/rollup/esbuild rely on that to drop unused modules.

maya: for edge specifically, prefer an ESM-only build that targets webcrypto. CJS builds often assume node globals (process, global, Buffer). can we ship two entrypoints: `edge` (esm, webcrypto) and `node` (cjs)? that avoids injecting node polyfills into edge bundles.

andrew: good call. but question: why did bundle include polyfills at all? I thought esbuild/rollup won't polyfill unless something imports it.

ethan: common reason — a CJS helper file contains an unconditional `require('crypto')` or references `global`. Even if unused by your code path, some bundlers can't entirely remove it if the package uses dynamic patterns. Also non-flat ESM/CJS interop -> bundler wraps CJS which references builtins, forcing shims.

samira: another gotcha: `package.json#exports` fallback to `require` can make bundlers resolve the CJS path instead of ESM. explicit conditional exports for `import` vs `require` helps. e.g.:
```
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
}
```

leo: and if you can't change upstream, you can alias problem imports in consumer bundler: `alias: { crypto: false }` or provide a small polyfill that maps to `globalThis.crypto.subtle` for edge. better: contribute a small PR to upstream to split polyfills into `polyfills/` so they are not pulled by default.

andrew: tried adding `sideEffects:false` locally and pointing exports to esm — bundle shrank ~800KB and deploy succeeded. thanks!

maya: nice. follow-ups: add a CI check that bundles a minimal edge sample app and fails if > X KB. also document the SDK packaging requirements in devex onboarding so sample apps don't accidentally import the CJS path.

ethan: +1. also remind maintainers to avoid `if (typeof window === 'undefined') require('something')` patterns that confuse static analysis. prefer dynamic import for conditionals: `if (something) await import('./node-only')` — bundlers can treat that as a split point.

samira: noted for the SDK checklist: export explicit ESM build, add `sideEffects:false`, move node-only code behind `require`/dynamic import or separate entry. add a tiny README section: "Edge compatibility" with examples for esbuild/webpack aliases.

deploy-bot: deploy failed for branch feature/edge-shrink — Vercel edge build error resolved after pushing 1769007801. :white_check_mark:

andrew: posting a short PR template in the repo to cover this. saving the analyzer output to the issue. thanks all! :pray:
